# Jacob Spon, *Miscellanea eruditae antiquitatis* (1685)

Primary-source pointer for the butterfly/soul iconography used in the LP1 p16 / LP2 p22 source investigation.

- Internet Archive scan: https://archive.org/details/gri_33125008544963
- Wikimedia Commons PDF record: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Miscellanea_eruditae_antiquitatis_-_in_quibus_marmora,_statuae,_musiva,_toreumata,_gemmae,_numismata,_Grutero,_Vrsino,_Boissardo_(IA_gri_33125008544963).pdf
- Contents entry: Art. III, “Nuptiae Cupidinis & Psyches, Papilio animae symbolum”, printed p. 7.

The commentary associated with the numbered figures identifies the butterfly as a symbol of the soul leaving the dead body (Table IV); describes a bird catching the butterfly as a figure of transmigration into animals (Table V); and describes Cupid fastening the soul to a tree with a nail so it cannot ascend (Table VI). These are the source's iconographic explanations, not cryptographic instructions.

Use the scan as a historical reference. The proposed correspondence between the LP1 p16 / LP2 p22 figure and Table IV is strong at the subject/composition level, but this note does not claim a pixel-verified crop lineage.
